walkthroughs.name: Why the coordinator has one door

beats.heading: Two callers, two ways in
beats.body: A pane's typed message goes straight to the linked thread as turn/start or turn/steer with the board's context, and its queue edits straight to the queue. Everything the coordinator asks goes through the four operations instead, one after another, so two of its effects never interleave and each is settled and reported in one place.

beats.heading: One turn at a time
beats.body: Codex runs one turn at a time on a thread and keeps what arrives meanwhile in the thread's own queue. A delegation to a busy workhorse joins that queue rather than starting a second turn, which would interleave two sets of edits to the same repository.

beats.heading: A start is a staged operation
beats.body: Opening a thread is staged in the epoch ledger before it is sent and committed after. A child that dies mid-flight leaves an operation whose outcome is stated as unknown rather than a binding nobody can account for.

beats.heading: The workhorse can reach the coordinator
beats.body: A workhorse starts with two reviewed tool manifests: archboard_app for the server's other threads and archboard_coordinator's tell_coordinator. The digest recorded for the start covers both, so changing what either tool tells the workhorse is a new manifest to review, not a silent edit.

beats.heading: A wait cannot close a cycle
beats.body: Every waiting tool registers its edge, so a thread waiting on something that is waiting on it is refused instead of hanging until a timeout nobody set.

beats.heading: Two callers, two ways in
beats.body: A pane's typed message goes straight to the workhorse of its checkout as turn/start or turn/steer with the board's context, and its queue edits go straight to that thread's queue. walkthroughs.name: Why the coordinator has one door

beats.heading: Two callers, two ways in
beats.body: A pane's typed message goes straight to the workhorse of its checkout as turn/start or turn/steer with the board's context, and its queue edits go straight to that thread's queue. Everything the coordinator asks goes through the four operations of the checkout it names instead, one after another, so two of its effects never interleave and each is settled and reported in one place.

beats.heading: One turn at a time
beats.body: Codex runs one turn at a time on a thread and keeps what arrives meanwhile in the thread's own queue. A delegation to a busy workhorse joins that queue rather than starting a second turn, which would interleave two sets of edits to the same repository.

beats.heading: A start is a staged operation
beats.body: Opening a thread is staged in the epoch ledger before it is sent and committed after. A child that dies mid-flight leaves an operation whose outcome is stated as unknown rather than a binding nobody can account for.

beats.heading: The workhorse can reach the coordinator

beats.heading: A wait cannot close a cycle
beats.body: Every waiting tool registers its edge, so a thread waiting on something that is waiting on it is refused instead of hanging until a timeout nobody set.

walkthroughs.name: Why the coordinator has one door

beats.heading: Two callers, two ways in
beats.body: A pane's typed message goes straight to the workhorse of its checkout as turn/start or turn/steer with the board's context, and its queue edits go straight to that thread's queue. Everything the coordinator asks goes through the four operations of the checkout it names instead, one after another, so two of its effects never interleave and each is settled and reported in one place.

beats.heading: One turn at a time
beats.body: Codex runs one turn at a time on a thread and keeps what arrives meanwhile in the thread's own queue. A delegation to a busy workhorse joins that queue rather than starting a second turn, which would interleave two sets of edits to the same repository.

beats.heading: A start is a staged operation
beats.body: Opening a thread is staged in the epoch ledger before it is sent and committed after. A child that dies mid-flight leaves an operation whose outcome is stated as unknown rather than a binding nobody can account for.

beats.heading: The workhorse can reach the coordinator
beats.body: A workhorse starts with two reviewed tool manifests: the host's own tools (archboard_app in Archboard) for the server's other threads, and tell_coordinator in the coordinator namespace the host names. The digest recorded for the start covers both, so changing what either tool tells the workhorse is a new manifest to review, not a silent edit.

beats.heading: A wait cannot close a cycle
beats.body: Every waiting tool registers its edge, so a thread waiting on something that is waiting on it is refused instead of hanging until a timeout nobody set.

nodes.name: Browser gateway
nodes.responsibility: Where a chat's command arrives, already admitted under its tab session's lease, and is carried out by the workhorse of the checkout the chat's tab shows
nodes.description: The gateway asks which checkout the chat's tab shows on every read and command, because the person can activate another one at any time: it hears the change and presents every chat of the tab again, with the workhorse of the new checkout. It dispatches each browser command to one action of that checkout's workhorse: a typed message or an interrupt (Stop) to the text actions (text-actions.ts), a queue edit to its queue, a new workhorse to its create action (thread-links.ts), which makes the tab's coordinator ready first. A command that names a thread is admitted only when that thread is the link of the shown checkout, and a lease taken before a switch is refused as link_changed. A command runs on the workhorse its lease was claimed for: once it has run, only that workhorse's own link is asked whether it still stands, so a switch meanwhile does not make its outcome unknown. None of them passes through the workhorse operations.

nodes.name: Coordinator tools
nodes.responsibility: The coordinator's tool calls: each becomes one of the four operations of the workhorse of the checkout the call names, or, for stop_workhorses, a stop of every workhorse of the tab
nodes.description: Each workhorse tool takes a required checkout, a directory the host admits, and the replay ledger counts the same arguments in another checkout as another call. A delegation to a checkout whose workhorse has no thread that can run turns starts it first; the other three tools refuse a checkout with no ready workhorse and say so. stop_workhorses names no checkout and no turn: it interrupts the running turn of every workhorse of the tab session, and says what each one did.

nodes.name: Workhorse operations
nodes.responsibility: The four things the coordinator may ask of a workhorse, one at a time: delegate, steer, inspect, manage its queue
nodes.description: The coordinator's one door in, and each workhorse has its own. Its operations run one after another, so two coordinator effects never interleave on one thread, and each mutation is staged, settled and reported under an epoch operation. A delegation starts a turn on an idle workhorse and joins the queue of an active one Archboard created. An operation follows its workhorse turn to the end even after a voice start replaces the coordinator that asked for it; only the current coordinator may start one.

nodes.name: Workhorse start
nodes.responsibility: Opens the thread one workhorse's link will name, with its instructions and both tool manifests, under a staged epoch operation
nodes.description: thread/start on gpt-6-astra at medium effort in the workhorse's checkout, which is the thread's working directory and workspace root, so it reads that repository's agent instructions and skills. It carries the workhorse developer instructions and the host's own tools (archboard_app in Archboard) and the coordinator namespace the host names (archboard_coordinator in Archboard); the manifest digest it records covers both.

nodes.name: Workhorse queue
nodes.responsibility: Codex's queue of messages waiting for the workhorse: list, add, edit, reorder, delete, or start one now
nodes.description: Each change is checked against the queue it expected before and after the remote effect. Codex itself runs one turn at a time and takes the next queued message when a turn ends.

nodes.name: Thread link
nodes.responsibility: Which workhorse each tab session and checkout is bound to, and the refusal when a second binding disagrees

nodes.name: Thread tools
nodes.responsibility: The archboard_app manifest a workhorse is started with, pinned by its digest

nodes.name: Shared instruction policy
nodes.responsibility: Compose core role rules, the host's toolset, turn input, context encoding, and exact immutable profile hashes

nodes.name: Epoch ledger
nodes.responsibility: Which child generation owns which thread, on disk, with operations that commit, roll back or say the outcome is unknown

nodes.name: Thread tool calls
nodes.responsibility: Runs the archboard_app calls a thread makes on the server's other threads: list, read, create, fork, message, and the waits
nodes.description: A creation, fork or message runs only once the user approves it, under the generation that may act; a wait registers its edges first. A thread it creates or forks works in the checkout of its caller, as the epoch ledger recorded it when the caller started.

nodes.name: Wait graph
nodes.responsibility: The wait edges every waiting tool registers, so a wait cannot close a cycle

nodes.name: Codex session
nodes.responsibility: The reviewed methods a turn is actually sent on

nodes.name: Tell coordinator
nodes.responsibility: The tell_coordinator tool of the coordinator namespace a workhorse is started with, named by the host: tell the coordinator one thing while it works
nodes.description: Its manifest is the reviewed template filled with the host's namespace and product name, pinned by the digest of those bytes. While voice is live, a call becomes workhorse news for the coordinator of the workhorse's tab session. With no voice session nothing is sent, and the workhorse is told nobody is listening.

nodes.name: Coordinator callbacks
nodes.responsibility: Deliver ordered workhorse news and a host's announced context changes to the voice coordinator and the voice
nodes.description: The shared runtime owns callback ordering, correlation, and delivery outcomes. A host announces its own context changes through the voice agent's announce, which gives the coordinator's and the voice's parts to this queue: Archboard announces its board changes, focus and selection. The tell_coordinator tool uses this same callback owner.

nodes.name: Session workhorses
nodes.responsibility: One workhorse for each checkout of a tab session: its starter, queue, operations and context delivery, built on first use
nodes.description: A workhorse works in its checkout, a directory the host admitted, and its thread-link key is the tab session and the checkout together. It belongs to the checkout, so it stays linked until its tab session ends. A stop for one checkout interrupts the turn that workhorse runs, and a stop for the tab interrupts the turn of every workhorse. The coordinator's stop_workhorses tool stops every running workhorse of the tab by voice.

nodes.name: Turns

nodes.name: Thread start
nodes.responsibility: Opens a workhorse's thread with its authored instructions and tool manifest, binds it to its tab session and checkout, and records which child generation owns it

nodes.name: Cross-thread calls
nodes.responsibility: Runs the archboard_app calls a thread makes on the server's other threads, and registers every wait so that no wait closes a cycle

nodes.name: Command admission

nodes.responsibility: Routes each admitted command to its account, thread, text, queue, approval or voice action

nodes.name: Operation lifecycle
nodes.responsibility: Stages operations, follows their workhorse turns and settles their outcomes once

nodes.name: Operations contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the requests, results and notifications of the four workhorse operations

nodes.name: Start contract
nodes.responsibility: Defines the starter port that exposes thread creation and its current snapshot

nodes.name: Thread start parameters
nodes.responsibility: Builds the thread start request with its checkout, instructions, tool manifests and reviewed model
